name: EU/EFTA Free Movement Permits (L/B/C EU/EFTA)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires EU/EFTA nationality. No quota and no labour-market test apply — this is registration-based, not application-based. An employment contract (or proof of self-employment plus sufficient means) is presented to the cantonal migration office/commune.

This requires registering with the canton within 14 days of arrival. Non-working persons must show sufficient means and comprehensive health insurance. Employment under 3 months/year needs no permit at all, just an employer online notification.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract or proof of self-employment/sufficient means

outcome.duration_length: L EU/EFTA: contract term (3-12 months); B EU/EFTA: 5 years; C EU/EFTA: indefinite

sources.title: Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons - State Secretariat for Migration

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL BASELINE for Switzerland's entire two-tier system: this route is registration-based, not application-based — no quota, no labour-market test, the near-opposite of ch_third_country_work_permit's restrictive quota system. C EU/EFTA settlement generally reaches 5 years for nationals of countries with a bilateral settlement/establishment treaty (commonly Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Liechtenstein, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain) — NOT a blanket EU/AFMP-wide entitlement, a genuine and common misconception on secondary sites this dataset exists to catch; the AFMP itself creates no settlement right at all, settlement is governed by FNIA plus separate settlement treaties. pr_after_months (60) and citizenship_after_months (120) reflect the standard case; treaty-nationality holders reach settlement faster (see ch_settlement_permit's nationality-dependent groups).
